title: Primitive recursiveness of the two-bit skipper
statement: For every predicate $v$ on pairs of Boolean values, the reader that consumes the first two bits when they satisfy $v$ and returns the remaining suffix, and otherwise fails, is primitive recursive.
hypotheses_covered: A predicate on pairs of Boolean values
replaced:
For every fixed test $v$ on pairs of Booleans, the skipping reader that consumes the
first two bits $a, b$ of a Boolean string and returns the remaining suffix when
$v(a, b)$ holds --- rejecting otherwise, and rejecting strings with fewer than two
bits --- is primitive recursive.
